newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Northam rises off low as shrinks losses.
newsitem.headline: Northam rises off low as shrinks losses.

text.p: Beleaguered South African platinum group Northam Platinum Ltd bounced off its 1997 low on Friday after it announced that it had reduced its losses in the second quarter of the year, dealers said.

By 1225 GMT Northam shares had added 16 cents or 8.4 percent to 206 cents, making it one of the biggest percentage gainers on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on the day. Volumes were, however, slim at 27,800.
"Northam has been suffering for such a long time that people are glad of any good news," one dealer said.
"Platinum is also a slightly safer place to be in than gold at the moment," he added.

Northam, part of the Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd stable, on Thursday reported a pre-capex loss to 0.63 million rand in the three months ended June 30 compared with the first quarter's 18.44 million rand loss.

Peter Janisch, executive director of Gold Fields's coal, base metals and platinum operations said that Northam had made use of the surge in platinum group metals prices in early June by selling metal they had in stock.
On June 6 the platinum price touched $500 an ounce.
He also said that it aimed to raise its milling rate and thereby hoped to insure profitability.
"We seem to be getting the mining operations right," Janisch said, adding however, that working costs in the past quarter were unfortunately higher than had been hoped.

Bullion last week sank to its lowest level in 12 years, spelling potential huge losses for the South African gold mining industry and layoffs of thousands of miners, analysts have said. -- Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
